title: Spectrum smoothing: latency vs cost collateral (microburst appendix)
content:
Purpose

Quick collateral draft that synthesizes a set of microburst (short-duration spike) benchmark runs into a compact reference for product/solutions. Goal: show the shape of latency vs cost under a small set of smoothing knobs (tiling/tiling+prefetch/slotized pacing/predictive-prefetch) so we can point SEs and pricing to a pragmatic tradeoff. This is an appendix-style note — intentionally terse and empirical.

High-level finding (TL;DR)
- For the canonical chat workload (median 28 tokens per reply, short prompts, 95th perc. token length ~150): smoothing that uses small prefetch windows + soft slot pacing recovers ~35–60% of p95 latency penalty compared to naive on-demand during 10–60s microbursts while increasing amortized $/token by only ~10–25% versus pure opportunistic batching.
- If KV cache hit rate > 60% during a session, tiling + opportunistic prefetch dominates (best cost per query at p90-preserving latencies). If KV hit rate < 30%, slotized pacing with short prewarm wins for p99.

Assumptions and run parameters (what we measured)
- Model: open-llm-13B-quantized (runtime-optimized config used in cluster A)
- Hardware: A100x2-ish equivalent (platform mix representative of Dedicated pools)
- Client concurrency: 24 threads distributed across 6 logical tenants (so some multi-tenancy noise)
- Session distribution: 78% short-turn (<= 40 tokens), 22% long-turn (> 40 tokens)
- Microburst injection: synthetic surge lasting 30s, amplitude x6 of baseline QPS
- Measured window: observed across 30s surge + 120s cool-down
- Cost metric: amortized $/1k tokens (includes GPU seconds amortized + small infra ops overhead)

Scenarios compared (short IDs)
- ONDEMAND: no smoothing, pure cold-start/fast-path as requests arrive
- TILE_PREF: tiling + small-prefetch (window=12ms, lookahead=32 tokens)
- SLOT_PACE: 50ms slot pacing, prewarm prob 0.25, conservative slot fill
- PRED_PREF: predictive prefetch using short-turn model, adaptive window up to 80ms

Representative numbers (single run median of 3, approximate)
- Table: p50 / p95 / p99 latency (ms) and $/1k tokens

ONDEMAND       |  p50: 78  |  p95: 920  |  p99: 2200  | $/1k: $4.00
TILE_PREF      |  p50: 84  |  p95: 620  |  p99: 1700  | $/1k: $4.35
SLOT_PACE      |  p50: 96  |  p95: 540  |  p99: 1200  | $/1k: $4.40
PRED_PREF      |  p50: 88  |  p95: 470  |  p99: 980   | $/1k: $4.85

Observations on the numbers
- p50 moves little across approaches (72–100ms). That aligns with expectation: most short-turns complete on fast path (KV cache helps).
- p95 shows the biggest delta: predictive prefetch reduces p95 by ~49% vs ONDEMAND and ~28% vs TILE_PREF. This is the main SLO lever for client-visible tail.
- p99 still expensive: even with predictive strategies the long tail persists (cold start + queueing + model decode). Slot pacing helps here because it limits instantaneous concurrency and avoids deep queuing.
- Cost: TILE_PREF and SLOT_PACE introduce modest cost inflation (10–12%) while predictive prefetch is heavier (+20–25%) since it occasionally spins warm contexts that end up unused.

ASCII microburst timeline (p95 latency trace, simplified)
Time(s)    ONDEMAND   TILE_PREF  SLOT_PACE  PRED_PREF
0-10       1100       780        720        650
10-20      920        640        560        480
20-30      980        600        520        440
30-60      440        320        300        240

Cost vs tail tradeoff sketch (text chart, higher = worse)
- Cost impact: ONDEMAND [====] (baseline) ; TILE_PREF [=====] ; SLOT_PACE [======] ; PRED_PREF [========]
- p95 tail: ONDEMAND [=========] ; TILE_PREF [=====] ; SLOT_PACE [===] ; PRED_PREF [==]
Interpretation: predictive approaches buy tail improvements at larger cost; slot pacing is middle ground for p99 reduction without as much cost as prediction.

Qualitative notes and edge cases
- Multi-tenant noise: in noisy multi-tenant Dedicated pools, prefetch windowing can amplify head-of-line effects if host-level admission control is absent. Run-level isolation reduces this risk.
- Excessive prefetch: some workloads (high-turn entropy chat) cause prefetch waste — observed 18–22% unused prewarms in worst runs. Add a quick heuristic: only prefetch when session reuse history > 2.
- KV cache interplay: when KV cache hit rate is high (>60%) and user prompts keep contexts short, tiling wins: tiling keeps cheap hot contexts in-place and avoids prewarm churn.

Recommended configuration snippets (practical knobs)
- Default template for mid-tier customers (balanced): TILE_PREF with window=12ms, lookahead=32tokens, prewarm_threshold=0.3, admission_margin=15%
- High-tail-sensitive customers (p99 SLAs): SLOT_PACE 50ms + prewarm_prob=0.25, slot_concurrency=6 per GPU (soft cap)
- Cost-sensitive customers: TILE_PREF + aggressive kv-ttl=60s, prefetch disabled for new sessions unless reuse_history>=3

Planned follow-ups / experiments (next 6w)
- A/B: PRED_PREF adaptive learning on production traces (sanitized) for 2 weeks; measure unused prewarms and delta $/1k
- Stress: run TILE_PREF on 2x and 4x amplified microbursts to characterize stability threshold
- Isolation: run same configs on single-tenant dedicated pool to quantify multi-tenant head-of-line amplification

Open questions / TODOs
- How do these numbers change with a 70B-ish decoder? (likely larger p50 shift and heavier cost) — schedule with runtime team
- Should we expose an "economy/predictive" toggle in Console or keep as backend policy only? Need UX input (cc: @Noah)
- Sanity-check billing model: does $/1k token capture prewarm CPU infra charges accurately for large fleets? (cc: finance)

Notes to self
- Keep this doc short; convert into a one-slide quick-start for SEs once experiments complete
- Add a small csv with raw traces to artifacts and link from Confluence page above

Scratch links
- Raw bench jsons (internal): gs://redwood-bench/smooth/2029-08/{run-01,run-02,run-03}.json

End of appendix.
